Resolves #19202

A claim on a `good first issue` or `help wanted` issue now gets an automatic reply within a minute, because no maintainer is online around the clock.
- **The reply:** either "first in line, you can start now; a maintainer confirms the assignment when one is online, which can take a while", or who holds the issue plus three claimable alternatives. The holder can be the assignee, an open PR that resolves it, or a live earlier claim.
- **What it never does:** assign anyone. A maintainer's confirmation stays the screen against accounts that spray claims.
- **Where the rules live:** a pure module, `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs`, with a spec. `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` only fetches and posts.

Evidence: L2 (the spec over the pure module, each rule mutation-tested) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-8, a live reply). An `issue_comment` run uses the default branch's workflow, so no reply can exist before merge. Residual: AC-1's live run and AC-8, Residual-Owner: #18985.

Review: full form. Workflows and security surfaces are never micro, and this workflow reads untrusted text with a write token.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered decision (`claimResponse.spec.mjs` › decideReply); the live one-minute reply is post-merge (see Post-Merge Validation) |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: › "the first claimant is first in line and may start now, with no promised time" (asserts no hour/day/minute in the text) |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: › isClaim (thank-you with quotes, questions, refusals, code) and › "no reply to the assignee, the team, a bot, a pull request, or an uncurated issue" |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: › "one reply per claimant"; plus the trigger is `created` only (edits never run) and runs are serialized per issue (`concurrency`) |
| AC-5 | Static, in the workflow: no assignment call, no `run:` step at all (the comment is read from `context.payload`), a sparse checkout of one file from the default branch, and every permission commented with its reason |
| AC-6 | CI-covered: › pickAlternatives (excludes the claimed issue, deterministic per claimant, different claimants get different first tickets); the workflow's query is `no:assignee -linked:pr` for the same label |
| AC-7 | `CONTRIBUTING.md` §3 item 3: "An automatic reply tells you whether you are first in line. If you are, the ticket is yours: start right away, and a maintainer confirms the assignment." (wording by @neo-opus-ada, the #18985 steward) |
| AC-8 | Post-merge (see Post-Merge Validation) |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Withdrawals free an issue, and an unassigned claim lapses after seven days**, matching CONTRIBUTING's seven days for a silent assignee. Without this, the ticket's own withdrawn-claim fixture would still hold its issue for everyone after it.
- **Holders are linked, never @-mentioned.** Otherwise an assignee would get a notification for every redirect. Only the claimant is mentioned.
- **Only a bot-authored marker counts as "already answered"**, so pasting the marker text cannot silence a reply to someone else.
- **A claimant's own open PR holds nothing against them.**
- The fixtures are the real threads with neutral handles. Public source should not name or label real contributors.

## Test Evidence
- Mutations, each restored byte-identical afterwards. Each one turns exactly one test red:
  - ignoring withdrawals
  - counting any marker
  - dropping the seven-day window
  - letting the claimant's own PR hold
  - keeping quoted lines
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/` locally: 834 passed.
- The workflow parses with `js-yaml`: `issue_comment` › `created`, with permissions `contents: read`, `issues: write` and `pull-requests: read`.
- agent-preflight: not hosted here (no `ai/` tree); the baseline jobs run in CI.

- [ ] A comment by a team member on a curated issue shows the job as skipped, because the `if:` does not match.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (non-blocking, watch): a holder is an assignee, a *linked* open PR, or a live earlier claim. A PR opened for the issue without a closing keyword is not linked, so `closedByPullRequestsReferences` does not see it and the next claimant hears "first in line" while work is in flight. That is the same gap the ticket names out of scope (the PR-side case), and the `no:assignee -linked:pr` alternatives query shares the blind spot. Not this PR's to fix; the day it recurs, the leaf should also read the "asked first" holder's own open PRs by author.
- **Challenge** (non-blocking, robustness): `earlierClaim` treats a withdrawal as freeing the issue only when it comes from the same login as the earlier claim, and `isWithdrawal` matches "please unassign me" and "consider it available" — a claimant who writes "I'll take this" and later "actually, no" (no pattern) still holds for seven days. Acceptable: the window bounds it, and a maintainer's assignment overrides everything.
- **Documented search:** (1) untrusted text reaching a shell or the reply — no `run:` step; the body enters only `isClaim`/`claimText` as a regex subject; the reply's dynamic parts are logins, numbers, constants; (2) the checkout ref — `actions/checkout@v7` with no `ref:` on an `issue_comment` run resolves the default branch, `persist-credentials: false`, sparse to the one module; (3) a re-run or a double claim answering twice — runs serialize per issue and only a bot-authored marker counts, so the second run sees the first's reply; (4) `author_association` on the payload comment and on `listComments` rows — both carry it, so the module's `isOutsideHuman` sees the same field the `if:` gate does; none found wanting.
